Location(s)
High Wycombe
Job Description
Engineering Manager, R&D — Material Characterization
PerkinElmer  |  High Wycombe, UK
Reports to:  Director, R&D — Material Characterization
Scope:  Line and delivery leadership of the multidisciplinary Material Characterization R&D engineering team — mechanical, optical, electronics, software and firmware — developing IR, UV-Vis and Thermal Analysis instruments (Fourier transform infrared spectrometers, UV-Visible spectrometers and differential scanning calorimeters).
Purpose of the role
Lead and develop the multidisciplinary engineering team responsible for the design, development and support of PerkinElmer’s Material Characterization hardware portfolio — high-precision optical and thermal-analysis instruments spanning optical benches, detectors and sources, precision mechanisms, embedded electronics and firmware, and instrument control software. The role owns the day-to-day of the engineering project portfolio — new product development, platform work and sustaining engineering — and is accountable for the capability, performance and growth of the team. Working closely with the Director of R&D and the Systems Engineering lead — who owns system architecture, requirements and design verification — the Engineering Manager is accountable for detailed discipline design, build and delivery, turning roadmap commitments into predictable, high-quality execution and building an environment where engineers do their best work.
Key responsibilities
1.  Team leadership and development
• Lead, coach and develop a multidisciplinary team of engineers across mechanical, optical, electronics, software and firmware disciplines.
• Own resource planning and allocation across projects; balance new product development, platform work and sustaining engineering.
• Recruit, retain and grow talent; build succession depth and technical capability across the team.
• Set clear objectives, give regular feedback and manage performance with a culture of accountability and continuous improvement.
2.  Delivery and execution
• Deliver projects to agreed scope, schedule, cost and quality; improve predictability through disciplined planning and risk management.
• Uphold phase-gate and design-review rigour in partnership with Systems Engineering; ensure detailed-design decisions are documented, reviewed and risk-assessed.
• Track and report progress, risks and mitigations to the Director of R&D and project stakeholders.
• Remove blockers and manage dependencies across disciplines, suppliers and partner sites.
3.  Engineering excellence and Design for Excellence
• Embed Design for Excellence — manufacturability, serviceability, reliability, quality, cost, sustainability and usability — in everyday engineering practice, including optical and precision-mechanical assemblies.
• Champion modular, reusable design across optical, precision-mechanical, electronic and firmware sub-systems, and reduce complexity across product families.
• Develop and maintain engineering processes, standards and tools that raise the quality and efficiency of the team’s output.
• Support value engineering and total cost of goods improvements without compromising customer outcomes.
4.  Cross-functional collaboration
• Work with Product Management, Science, Systems Engineering, Operations, Quality, Service and Supply Chain to deliver products that succeed commercially and operationally.
• Translate customer and business needs into engineering plans and priorities with the Director of R&D and Product Management.
• Support manufacturing transfer, supplier qualification, alternative sourcing and resolution of production and field issues.
5.  Quality, compliance and continuous improvement
• Ensure compliance with quality, regulatory and product-development requirements.
• Capture and apply learning from development, launch, production and the field.
• Promote appropriate IP generation and protection.
First 90 days
• Understand current projects, priorities, risks and roadmap commitments; build relationships across the team and with key stakeholders.
• Assess team capability, workload and succession risk; agree development and hiring priorities with the Director of R&D.
• Review project execution, design-review and planning practices; identify near-term opportunities to improve predictability.
• Take ownership of in-flight deliverables and establish a clear reporting rhythm with the Director of R&D and project stakeholders.
Qualifications and experience
Essential
• Degree in Engineering, Physics or a related technical discipline.
• Significant experience developing complex, high-precision optical, electro-mechanical or scientific instrumentation in an industrial R&D environment.
• Proven line management or team leadership of multidisciplinary engineering teams.
• Track record of delivering products from concept through launch and sustaining support within a structured product-development framework.
• Strong planning, communication and stakeholder-management skills.
Preferred
• Advanced degree (MSc, PhD) or equivalent experience.
• Domain knowledge of optical, spectroscopic or thermal-analysis instrumentation and the underlying physics and engineering — optical-bench design, detectors and sources, precision mechanisms, embedded control, thermal management and signal processing.
• Experience with modular architecture, platform development and Design for Excellence methodologies.
• Familiarity with hybrid Agile and phase-gate delivery models and modern engineering toolchains.
• Experience working across sites and suppliers in a global, matrixed organisation.

Job Description:
Job Summary
We are looking for a Product Engineer to join our AI Search and Retrieval Context Engineering as we build the next generation of legal AI experiences for law firms.
This is not a traditional front-end developer role where requirements are handed over and built from a specification. It is a hands-on product engineering role for someone who can understand the problem, shape the user experience, think through the system design and then build high-quality software.
The role is primarily focused on React, TypeScript and modern user experience development, but the expectation is broader than UI delivery. You will work close to lawyers, knowledge teams, innovation teams and technical stakeholders to understand how AI search, retrieval and agents should fit into real legal workflows.
We are not building another disconnected AI chatbot. We are building trusted AI experiences that sit on top of the firm’s own documents, knowledge, matters, metadata and workflows.
As a Product Engineer, you will help turn complex AI retrieval capability into simple, useful and trusted experiences for lawyers.
Why This Role Matters
AI is changing software engineering. The value of an engineer is no longer only in writing code quickly. AI can now help generate code, tests and components at speed. That makes the human part of engineering more important, not less.
The best engineers are now the ones who understand the system, the user, the constraints and the business problem.
For this team, that means understanding why a lawyer is searching, what they need to trust an answer, what happens if the wrong document is surfaced, how permissions work, how citations should be displayed, and how the experience fits into their daily workflow.
A button is not just a button. A search result is not just a card. An AI answer is not just text on a page.
In legal AI, every interaction has to support trust, explainability, security and adoption.
That is why we need Product Engineers: people who are fluent in engineering, fluent in product thinking, and willing to understand the domain deeply enough to build the right thing.
About the Team
The Search & AI team helps law firms build secure, firm-specific AI capabilities on top of their existing document, knowledge and matter infrastructure.
We work with firms that want to move beyond standalone AI tools and create a trusted AI layer inside their own environment. Our solutions typically connect to systems such as iManage, SharePoint, NetDocuments, Microsoft 365, Azure AI Search, Azure OpenAI and internal knowledge platforms.
The team already has experience delivering AI search and workflow capabilities for a Magic Circle law firm and a global multinational law firm, including natural language search, agents and Azure-based retrieval solutions built in partnership with Microsoft.
As the market shifts from AI adoption to AI ownership, our team is becoming more like a Forward Deployment Engineering function: technical people who work close to strategic clients, understand their workflows, and build real solutions that move from prototype to production.
The Role
You will design and build the product experience layer for legal AI.
That includes search interfaces, AI answer experiences, document previews, citation views, agent workflows, feedback loops, dashboards, admin screens and embedded components for tools lawyers already use.
You will mainly work in React and TypeScript, building polished, enterprise-grade applications that are fast, accessible, secure and suitable for professional legal users.
You will work with AI engineers, retrieval architects, Azure engineers, legal knowledge experts and client stakeholders to turn complex technical capabilities into clear, usable products.
What You Will Build
You may build a natural language search experience that allows lawyers to ask questions across a firm’s knowledge bank and receive grounded answers with citations.
You may create a source preview panel that lets a lawyer inspect the exact document behind an AI answer before relying on it.
You may design an agent workflow where a lawyer can run a research task, review retrieved documents, refine the question, compare outputs and export the result.
You may build dashboards that show search quality, adoption, answer confidence, feedback trends and retrieval performance.
You may create embedded components for SharePoint, Teams, Word, Outlook or a firm intranet, so AI appears inside the workflow rather than as another destination.
The common thread is that you will be building the experience layer that makes AI usable, explainable and trusted.
Key Responsibilities
Build high-quality React and TypeScript applications
You will build modern front-end applications using React, TypeScript and strong component design. You will care about performance, accessibility, responsiveness, error handling, loading states, empty states, maintainability and the overall quality of the user experience. You will work with APIs, authentication, permissions, search services, AI responses, document metadata and workflow actions.
Shape the product, not just the code
You will help define how legal AI experiences should work. This means challenging unclear requirements, simplifying complex workflows, proposing better interaction patterns and making sure the team is building something users will actually adopt. You will not just wait for a perfect specification. You will help create it.
Understand the lawyer workflow
You will work close to legal users and client teams to understand how lawyers search for knowledge, review documents, validate answers and move through their work. The goal is to build AI into workflows lawyers already understand, rather than sending them to another disconnected tool.
Turn AI retrieval into trusted UX
You will design interfaces that make retrieval transparent. This includes citations, source previews, metadata, snippets, filters, document cards, confidence signals, feedback mechanisms and audit-friendly interaction patterns. In legal AI, the user needs to understand where an answer came from and why it should be trusted.
Work across the system
Although this is mainly a React and TypeScript role, you will need to understand how your UI fits into the wider system. That may include Azure AI Search, Azure OpenAI, retrieval APIs, MCP-style tool access, document processing pipelines, security trimming, Microsoft Graph, SharePoint, iManage or other enterprise…

The Role
As Project Engineer, you'll act as the technical link between design and construction across Access, Ground Investigation (GI), PRI, Overhead Line (OHL) and associated civil engineering works. You'll ensure that designs are practical, information is complete and construction teams have everything they need to deliver safely and efficiently.
You'll play a key role in identifying technical risks early, resolving engineering issues and ensuring work packages are fully coordinated before they reach site.
What You'll Be Doing
• Coordinate day-to-day engineering activities between designers, subcontractors, site teams and project management.
• Ensure drawings, specifications, surveys, ground investigation information and approvals are available before construction starts.
• Review upcoming work packages, identifying missing information, technical constraints and constructability issues.
• Raise and manage Technical Queries (TQs), Requests for Information (RFIs) and design clarifications through to resolution.
• Coordinate engineering interfaces across access roads, drainage, earthworks, structures, platforms, Overhead Lines (OHL) and temporary works.
• Support design reviews, constructability reviews and technical handovers into construction.
• Identify design or site changes that impact scope, programme or cost, supporting the project change control process.
• Assist with inspections, quality hold points and the resolution of technical defects or non-conformances.
• Work closely with the Temporary Works Coordinator to ensure temporary works are correctly designed, approved and implemented.
• Maintain accurate red-line drawings, as-built records and engineering handover documentation.
• Report on technical risks, outstanding design information and overall workface readiness.
About You
You'll be a technically strong engineer with experience delivering complex infrastructure or civil engineering projects. You'll enjoy working collaboratively, be confident interpreting engineering information and have the ability to identify and resolve issues before they affect programme or construction.

• Experience as a Project Engineer, Site Engineer, Design Engineer or Design Coordinator on major infrastructure projects.
• Strong technical understanding of engineering drawings, specifications, calculations and construction documentation.
• Practical knowledge of construction sequencing, constructability, temporary works and site engineering practices.
• Experience managing technical queries, design changes, inspections and engineering close-out activities.
• Good understanding of CDM Regulations, Safety by Design principles and engineering quality assurance processes.
It Would Be Great If You Also Have
• Incorporated or Chartered Engineer status, or be working towards professional registration.
• Membership of a recognised engineering institution.
• Experience within electricity transmission and distribution, overhead line or utilities infrastructure.
• Knowledge of access roads, drainage, earthworks, structures, bridges, culverts, platforms or ground investigation.
• Familiarity with NEC contracts and Common Data Environments (CDE).
Why Join United Living Infrastructure?
At United Living Infrastructure, you'll be part of a collaborative team delivering nationally significant infrastructure projects that make a real difference.

If you're looking for a role where you can influence project delivery, solve complex engineering challenges and see your work make a lasting impact, we'd love to hear from you.
Join us at United Infrastructure and be part of our mission to deliver innovative and sustainable solutions to the complex infrastructure needs of the UK.

Reed in Partnership has been delivering public services since 1998. We are a British, family-owned company, whose mission has always been to positively transform people and their communities. This is reflected in our services, which we deliver to help people from all backgrounds and circumstances to change their lives for the better.

£30,000 - £31,500
Job Description
Are you passionate about making a difference and helping others to fulfil their potential?
Would you like to work in a role that puts the customer at the heart of everything we do, making a genuine positive impact?
Then consider the role of Employment Adviser at Reed in Partnership!
Please note, internal applications for this role close on 08/10/26
Who we are:
Reed in Partnership's Employability Division aims to positively transform lives by helping individuals who are unemployed, economically inactive, or facing challenges such as health conditions, disabilities, or caring responsibilities to find sustainable employment. Through a wide range of tailored support services including one-to-one careers guidance, CV writing, interview preparation, and skills training, we have supported over 250,000 people on their journey into work.
Our Restart Scheme, funded by the Department for Work and Pensions (DWP), focuses specifically on supporting the long-term unemployed who are referred and mandated to the scheme by their local Job Centre Plus. We provide them with up to 12 months of personalised support to enter or re-enter the workforce.
What is the role about?
Employment Advisers are the front line of Reed in Partnership, directly contributing to our mission by supporting jobseekers (our participants), engaging with local employers, and promoting the benefits of the Restart Scheme within the local community. Our participants are the lifeblood of our business and providing them with an excellent service is at the very core of the Employment Adviser role.
Please note this role requires travel to our Hemel office.
Just some of your day-to-day responsibilities will include:
Taking Ownership
• Meeting with and supporting a caseload of long-term unemployed jobseekers, identifying their barriers and creating tailored action plans to progress them into employment.
• Delivering personalised, one-to-one guidance to our participants including CV writing, interview preparation, and skills development.
• Meeting and exceeding performance targets and Key Performance Indicators (KPIs).
Working Together
• Collaborating with participants to shift their mindset and build the confidence they need to find and sustain work.
• Engaging with local employers to identify job opportunities.
• Signposting participants to internal and external stakeholders to address specific barriers such as health, housing, or financial challenges.
• Promoting the Restart Scheme within the community, raising awareness of it's benefits and impact.
Being Fair, Open, and Honest
• Providing inclusive support and advice to people from all backgrounds.
What’s in it for you?
A generous base salary (pro-rata for part time), and great flexibility with your working schedule, we offer training, development and progression opportunities. You will have access to the range of Reed in Partnership benefits, which include:
• 25 days annual leave (pro-rata for part time) plus statutory bank holidays
• Reed Pension Scheme
• Award Winning Management & Leadership training
• Professional & Personal Development Funds
• Bi-annual pay reviews
• Plus much more that can be found on our website.
The Employment Adviser role offers immense satisfaction of connecting people with the tailored support that they need to fulfil their potential. At Reed in Partnership, our values - Fair, Open & Honest, Take Ownership, and Work Together - guide everything we do. Join us in delivering services that make a real difference.
To be successful in this role, we are looking for someone with:
• Ability to demonstrate coaching/mentoring experience and persuasion/influencing skills through previous work or social activities.
• Experience of working in a customer facing environment (i.e. Customer Services, Hospitality, Social Care, Customer Services, Sales)
• Experience of working in a fast paced, performance target driven environment.
• Willingness to travel locally (e.g. to meet customers/employers).
• A minimum of 2 A-Levels or an equivalent Level 3 Diploma.
• GCSE English Language at a minimum of a Grade B (or equivalent Level 2 qualification). OR achievement of a Level 2 in Literacy Assessment at interview stage OR International Equivalents.
Desirable Criteria:
• Fluency in more than one language
We aim to ensure that no candidate or employee receives less favourable treatment on the grounds of gender, race, disability, sexual orientation, religion or belief, age, gender reassignment, marital or civil partnership status, pregnancy or maternity.  We offer a guaranteed interview scheme for disabled applicants who meet the minimum criteria.

Do you want to help us improve human health and understand life on Earth? Make your mark by shaping the future to enable or deliver life-changing science to solve some of humanity’s greatest challenges.
We are seeking a highly motivated and creative Postdoctoral Fellow to join the Martin group at the Wellcome Sanger Institute, working towards understanding the genetic basis of early-life traits and conditions, and/or to develop biomarkers for pregnancy complications and neonatal diseases.
About the Group:
The Martin group works on the genetic basis of rare and common disease, using large-scale human genetic datasets with rich linkage to electronic health records and questionnaires. Over the last few years, we have had a particular emphasis on the genetics of neurodevelopmental disorders and related traits, the genetics of complex disease in populations with high levels of consanguinity, and factors influencing germline mutation rates. Recent work from the group has appeared in Nature, Cell, Nature Genetics, and Nature Human Behavior. A full list of our recent papers can be found here: https://www.sanger.ac.uk/group/martin-group/. The group is now opening new research directions involving genomics and multi-omics in very early life. Most conditions in the earliest stages of life remain untouched by large-scale genomics, and molecular predictors that could guide clinical management are urgently needed. We are building a programme spanning a clinical continuum from pregnancy loss, through fetal growth restriction, to complications of premature birth. This includes large-scale sequencing of birth cohorts to study the genetic basis of perinatal and early-life traits and conditions, genetic and multi-omic studies of neonatal conditions using nationwide Scandinavian dried blood spots, and large-scale sequencing of cell-free DNA (cfDNA) from pregnant mothers.
What you'll be doing:
We are seeking a highly motivated postdoc to work on one or more of the following projects:
• Analysis of large-scale proteomic data from nationwide Scandinavian dried blood spots, in order to develop biomarkers for understudied neonatal conditions that are common in premature babies. These samples are collected before disease onset and linked to rich registry data, which opens up questions about molecular subtypes, prediction and aetiology that have not previously been tractable. There may also be the opportunity to analyse largescale genetic datasets from these same blood spots, to carry out the first well-powered genetic studies of these neonatal conditions.
• Analysis of new sequence and genotype data from over 110,000 individuals across four birth cohorts, including the Norwegian Mother, Father and Child Cohort Study (MoBa), to explore genetic influences on neurodevelopmental and perinatal traits. This is one of the world’s largest family-based sequence datasets. Questions here could include:
• Disentangling direct from indirect genetic effects using new methods. Exploring time-varying effects of genetics using longitudinal phenotype data.
• Exploring the factors influencing penetrance of variants associated with rare neurodevelopmental conditions.
• Studying how genetic architecture of different traits varies across the phenotype distribution.
• Developing biomarkers for pregnancy complications from methylation-aware whole-genome sequence data on cell-free DNA (cfDNA) from pregnant women, including methods development to incorporate both epigenetic and genetic information in the same assay.
Questions here could include:
• Disentangling direct from indirect genetic effects using new methods. Exploring time-varying effects of genetics using longitudinal phenotype data.
• Exploring the factors influencing penetrance of variants associated with rare neurodevelopmental conditions.
• Studying how genetic architecture of different traits varies across the phenotype distribution.
• Developing biomarkers for pregnancy complications from methylation-aware wholegenome sequence data on cell-free DNA (cfDNA) from pregnant women, including methods development to incorporate both epigenetic and genetic information in the same assay.
This project is also listed in the parallel advert for our cfDNA-focused postdoctoral position, and could be taken forward from either post. The project can be tailored around the postdoc's interests and expertise. The work will be done in collaboration with groups in the UK, Scandinavia and elsewhere, as well as with other groups at the Sanger Institute.
About you:
This role would suit someone with experience in statistical analyses of large-scale human genetic or other omic datasets, particularly on DNA sequence data, methylation data and/or with high-throughput proteomic data. You will be based at the Wellcome Sanger Institute on the Wellcome Genome Campus near Cambridge, with access to world-leading sequencing capacity and computational infrastructure, and to a large community of statistical and computational geneticists. You will join the Postdoctoral Fellow community and be able to take part in training, networking opportunities. Prospective candidates are welcome to contact hcm@sanger.ac.uk with informal queries before deciding whether to apply.
Essential Skills:
• PhD in a relevant area (statistics, statistical genetics, genetics, genomics, proteomics, bioinformatics or similar)
• Experience analysing large-scale high-throughput human genetic and/or epigenetic and/or proteomic data, including quality control and normalization where relevant
• Knowledge of statistical methods appropriate for large-scale omics research
• Full working proficiency in Python and/or R, and Unix/Linux
• Experience or enthusiasm for using AI tools to improve productivity in scientific research
• Previous experience writing highly reproducible code with github, Snakemake/Nextflow, RMarkdown or similar
• Creativity and original scientific ideas
• Enthusiasm and commitment
• Attention to detail
• Strong problem-solving skills
• Ability to communicate ideas and results effectively both verbally and in writing
• Ability to prioritise, work independently and organise own workload
• Ability to collaborate effectively with and independently supervise less experienced scientists
Other information:

Job Description
The Marketing Engagement Lead owns the local customer engagement strategy for assigned brand(s), translating Takeda’s central brand strategy and modular content into a locally executable, omnichannel plan, and delivers local brand performance anchored in Takeda’s values of Patient, Trust, Reputation and Business.
Key objectives
• Own the local customer engagement strategy for assigned brand(s), translating Takeda’s central brand strategy and modular content into a locally executable plan.
• Design the customer journey and orchestrate omnichannel engagement across field and non-personal channels, managing local investment on an ROI basis.
• Feed performance, market and customer insights back to Marketing & Commercial Excellence (MCE) to shape future brand strategy and content.
• Serve as the local expert on the NHS/HSE operating environment, using internal and external insight sources to shape a UK/IE-fit engagement and brand plan.
• Deliver local brand performance — market competitiveness and financial results — anchored in Takeda’s values of Patient, Trust, Reputation and Business.
Responsibilities
• Own the Local Engagement Plan — an all-channel, all-tactic plan covering segments, objectives, channel mix and sequencing, module selection, budget, enablement, measurement and learning agenda — developed with cross-functional buy-in.
• Lead local brand planning inputs, ensuring customer engagement activity is connected to brand strategy, commercial objectives, launch priorities and lifecycle opportunities.
• Conduct local situational analysis and customer insight to ground the engagement strategy (engagement-focused, not brand re-strategizing).
• Design the local HCP/customer journey and experience across touchpoints, optimising engagement quality rather than activity volume.
• Select, adapt and prioritise the elements of Takeda’s central MCE strategy that best meet the needs of UK & IE customers and the local healthcare system.
• Set engagement objectives, target audiences, key messages and content needs across face-to-face (field/KAM), many-to-many (meetings, congresses, advisory boards) and digital/non-personal channels.
• Brief and train field teams on brand messaging and narrative; the Sales Lead owns field-team management, coaching and delivery.
• Orchestrate cross-functional engagement — convene and align commercial, medical and access partners, leading or co-leading the local engagement team while respecting compliance processes and SOPs.
• Apply a reuse-first, modular-content approach via the Takeda Content Factory; localise only where required within approved claims and run efficient local MLR.
• Use data, analytics and AI-enabled orchestration (next-best-action / decision engines, CRM) to interpret performance and personalise engagement.
• Manage and optimise the local engagement investment and partner with Finance and Supply on forecasting and demand planning.
• Support launch excellence and lifecycle management by coordinating local readiness, performance tracking, optimisation and post-launch learning.
• Close the loop — convert performance data into next-wave optimisation and structured insight, content/module gaps and recommendations back to MCE.
Ensuring compliance with the following regulations / requirements:
• All applicable laws, regulations and industry codes (e.g. EFPIA and the relevant national pharmaceutical industry code).
• Takeda’s policies, SOPs and ethical standards.
• Medical, Legal and Regulatory (MLR) review processes, and the separation of promotional and medical/scientific engagement.
Key Requirements
Qualifications
• Relevant degree (e.g. life sciences, marketing or business). Specific requirements confirmed locally.
• Advanced qualification (e.g. postgraduate degree) an advantage.
Experience
• Proven experience in pharmaceutical / healthcare marketing, customer engagement or omnichannel activation.
• Experience localising central strategy and content, and orchestrating cross-functional, omnichannel engagement.
• Experience contributing to brand planning, launch preparation, launch execution and lifecycle management in a local pharmaceutical market.
• Experience managing activity budgets within compliance / MLR processes.
• Strong understanding of the UK/IE NHS/HSE operating environment and its implications for customer engagement, access, adoption and brand performance.
Skills/Competencies
• Data, analytics and AI fluency (next-best-action, decision engines, CRM).
• Modular-content and MLR literacy with a reuse-first mindset.
• Matrix leadership and cross-functional orchestration; strong influencing and stakeholder management.
• Strategic brand planning, launch excellence and lifecycle management capability, with the ability to connect customer engagement to commercial outcomes.
• Agile, test-and-learn ways of working.
Disposition:
• Role-models Takeda’s six culture pillars: Patient-Centric, People-Minded, Respectful & Collaborative, Decision Effectiveness, Performance Culture and Enterprise Orientation.
• Patient-centred and values-led (Patient, Trust, Reputation, Business); debates then commits, and decides with speed while managing risk and compliance.
• Enterprise-first mindset; embraces change and takes calculated, compliant risks to improve engagement and outcomes.
Complexity and Problem Solving
This role operates in a fast-moving omnichannel environment and is expected to:
• Balance central strategy and content with local execution, and the separation of promotional vs medical / scientific engagement, across multiple channels and brands.
• Translate NHS/HSE environment dynamics, local customer needs and external market signals into practical choices on strategy adaptation, launch execution and lifecycle optimisation.
• Navigate compliance constraints (MLR, SOPs, local codes) while acting with pace to deliver measurable results.
• Operate with autonomy within a defined scope, making and being accountable for decisions that affect the country / LOC, assigned brand(s) results and customer outcomes.
• Apply Takeda’s decision framework — balancing Patient, Trust, Reputation and Business priorities — and respect decision roles (Decide / Advise / Inform).
Internal and External Contacts
• Internal: local cross-functional engagement team (commercial, medical, access); central Marketing & Commercial Excellence (Strategy & Marketing, Marketing Execution, Commercial Capabilities); Sales; Finance; Supply; DD&T and Insights & Analytics.
• External: priority customers and healthcare professionals (HCPs); external partners and agencies as required.

Salesforce is the #1 AI CRM, where humans with agents drive customer success together. Here, ambition meets action. Tech meets trust. And innovation isn’t a buzzword — it’s a way of life. The world of work as we know it is changing and we're looking for Trailblazers who are passionate about bettering business and the world through AI, driving innovation, and keeping Salesforce's core values at the heart of it all.
Ready to level-up your career at the company leading workforce transformation in the agentic era? You’re in the right place! Agentforce is the future of AI, and you are the future of Salesforce.
As a Principal AI Architect (or AI and Data Technical Architect), you will act as a senior, hands-on technical leader and trusted advisor to our customers. You will be responsible for designing, validating, and operationalizing enterprise-grade data and AI architectures centered on Salesforce D360 and the Agentforce platform. This role sits at the intersection of data engineering, platform architecture, and applied AI, requiring you to guide customer Chief Data Officers and Enterprise Architects through emerging AI solutions. You will work side-by-side with Account Executives and Product teams to ensure customers realize the full value of the platform by designing scalable, secure solutions that integrate D360 into complex enterprise ecosystems—including hyperscalers, data lakes, and governance frameworks.
Responsibilities
• Lead pre-sales technical design by analyzing customer needs and recommending solutions aligned with Agentforce capabilities and integration with external agent frameworks.
• Shape best practices around generative AI, agent interoperability, prompt engineering, Data Cloud, and cross-platform integrations.
• Collaborate with AEs and SEs to build hands-on prototypes and demos using Agentforce and integrated external agents.
• Develop thought leadership content—demo templates, whitepapers, enablement sessions—focused on agent lifecycle, integration strategy, and technical effectiveness.
• Act as a central technical knowledge resource, proactively addressing internal technical inquiries, facilitating deep technical enablement, and documenting best practices to empower specialist teams across the organization.
• If you are naturally curious about AI and Data, love diving into new technologies, and enjoy educating others while crafting solutions that deliver real business impact, we want to talk to you!
• Understand Agent Interoperability - Map and integrate external agents from hyperscalers (e.g. Copilot, Gemini) into Agentforce via open standards (MCP, A2A); design how these systems collaborate.
• Enable Conversational & Background Agents - Use Agentforce Studio and Agent Builder to configure chat and background agents; integrate with external channels including voice via hyperscaler APIs.
• Drive Prompt Engineering & Lifecycle Strategy - Lead prompt design, testing, monitoring, and iteration; define agent lifecycle best practices from development through refinement.
• Build Hands-On Demos & Prototypes - Co-create quick prototypes (<2 weeks) with AEs demonstrating integration between Agentforce and external agents or services.
• Lead Pre-Sales Workshops - Facilitate whiteboarding, deep-dive sessions, and quick enablement for customers and internal teams.
• Advise on Data & Integration - Integrate Data Cloud (D360), CRM, MuleSoft APIs, and external agent endpoints ensuring cohesive architectures that align with compliance and governance policies.
• Support Early Adoption - Occasionally assist in proof-of-value engagements post-sale by tuning agents and guiding customers toward self-sufficient enablement.
• Own Technical Architecture Decisions - Oversee data modeling, identity resolution, real-time vs. batch patterns, data graph design, and activation strategies within D360.
• Own Technical Enablement - Create and manage accessible technical documentation, knowledge bases, and FAQ resources to rapidly resolve internal technical inquiries, empowering specialist teams to handle technical discussions confidently.

• Enterprise AI & Hyperscaler Ecosystem Depth: Proven experience designing and delivering AI, GenAI, and Data architectures within platforms such as AWS (Bedrock/SageMaker), Microsoft (Azure AI Foundry/Copilot), Databricks, Google Cloud (Vertex AI), Snowflake, or Palantir.
• Hands-On Modern AI & Agentic Builder Experience: Direct hands-on experience building, prototyping, or solutioning with frontier LLMs and modern AI tools—including OpenAI, Claude, LangChain / LangGraph, Cursor, or multi-agent orchestration frameworks.
• Agent Interoperability & Open Standards: Experience with Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG), prompt engineering, background/conversational agents, voice AI integrations, or open protocols (e.g., Model Context Protocol - MCP, A2A).
• Rapid Prototyping & Whiteboarding: Demonstrated ability to lead technical discovery workshops and co-create rapid proof-of-value prototypes (<2 weeks) for C-suite stakeholders (CDO, CTO, Enterprise Architects).
• Location: Based in London, UK (hybrid model).
Preferred Qualifications (Nice-to-Have):
•
• CRM / Salesforce Context: Prior familiarity or hands-on experience with Salesforce CRM, Agentforce Studio, or Data Cloud (D360).
• Multi-Modal & Advanced AI Frameworks: Experience with voice pipelines, MLOps, vector search, or custom model fine-tuning.

The Role
The Product Manager is responsible for the product vision through to implementation alongside our development teams. They will work with business development teams to identify product-market fit, engage with prospects and customers to deeply understand the problems they have and how we can help solve these problems. They will become the expert on how clients use the product and evangelise their products internally and with clients. They will use client feedback, metrics and research to identify and prioritise opportunities for delivering enhancements and new product ideas.
Based on the wider product strategy and input from commercial and technical teams, the Product Manager will define a long-term vision for the product, convey this to the wider business, and propose new initiatives to grow the value proposition of their products while at the same time making meaningful progress towards their longer term vision for the product or products.
Once the vision is defined; the Product Manager will play a crucial part in product delivery. They will fulfil the product owner role within one or more agile delivery teams, creating a shared understanding of client needs. They will define the priorities and clear acceptance criteria for designing and implementing new features and improvements. They will be responsible for prioritisation and will strive to find the right balance between maintenance, customer requests, and advancing the strategic product roadmap.
The Product Manager will motivate technical teams by being the voice of the customer. They will share client insights, needs, frustrations, successes and failures with the team to inspire a culture of creative problem solving. They will hold themselves and the team accountable for delivering client value and will use excellent communication skills to ensure internal and external stakeholders are kept up-to-date throughout product delivery. Rather than simply adopting a "Clients say they want this so we did it" mindset, they will strategically evaluate how small requests add up to something bigger over time.
Responsibilities
• Customer engagement: The Product Manager is expected to build client relationships to facilitate idea generation and be the expert on how the clients use the system, understand their requirements and become the voice of the customer internally. They are expected to be proactive in terms of seeking out new relationships and identify customer needs outside of our core customer set.
• Bring new features to the market: The Product Manager should spend time with clients and internal sales and support teams, providing assistance, engagement and gaining understanding of the products.
• Internal team engagement: Establish strong cross functional relationships (e.g., Support, Development, QA, Client Management); regularly engage across functions to leverage areas knowledge, facilitate information sharing, and accelerate product delivery.
• Synthesize and document requirements: Develop high level Epic stories and break those down into detailed user stories.  During development of new functionality the PO will work closely with multiple teams, to break down stories and develop acceptance tests to ensure client requirements are successfully captured and implemented.
• Build client workflows intelligence library: PMs are expected to become specialists and an authoritative source for the rest of the business for the understanding of client workflows. Special emphasis will be placed on effective documentation, dissemination and sharing of this knowledge across the Product team and the rest of the company.
• Trayport network fluency: Become an expert on the usage of Trayport’s products/network in ‘the wild’ and provide a bridge between customers and Trayport engineering teams regarding workflows, requirements and platform functionality, for existing and components/features in development.
• Advocacy of the product: Run demos of new and existing functionality, internally and externally, participate in customer facing calls and meetings to gather requirements and present prototypes.
The Person
Skills & Experience
• Experience working with Data and AI products in the commodities space
• A solid understanding of what data is important to trading firms (and more crucially what is not) especially in the energy trading space
• Able to demonstrate a keen understanding how how trading firms leverage agentic AI at present
• Solid technical skills for data analysis (e.g. Python, SQL, etc.)
• Strong internal and client-facing communication
• Well versed engaging with customers to understand their needs, validate ideas, communicate the value proposition and manage expectations
• Executing cross-functional initiatives
• Making decisions based on qualitative and quantitative insights
• Creating and presenting business cases, defining outcome-based success criteria
Personal Attributes
• Effective communicator with strong interpersonal skills
• Driven, client-centric and outcome-focused
• Naturally curious, always seeking new knowledge

Dual Fuel Smart Meter Engineer
Locations: DL, DH, NE, SR, TS
Are you a qualified Dual Fuel Smart Meter Engineer looking for excellent earning potential, structured work and the security of working directly for an established energy supplier?
At Utilita, we're growing our award-winning Field Services team. Join one of the UK's fastest-growing energy suppliers and a business that has been recognised as one of the UK's Top 50 Best Workplaces for four consecutive years.
What is in it for you?
You'll receive a base salary of £38,993, alongside uncapped earning potential and a variety of opportunities to boost your overall earnings, including:
• On-call payment: Receive £330 for each on-call week, based on an average rota of one week in five. (OTE of £42,293 just with the base salary and conducting mandatory on call requirements)
• Industry-leading installation bonus: Benefit from an uncapped installation bonus of £25 per meter or £50 per dual installation once you have completed a minimum of four installations in a day, with additional work opportunities available to further enhance your earnings.
• London weighting: Receive an additional £2,000 annual allowance if you live within the M25.
• Enhanced overtime: Enhanced overtime rates for Sunday working.
Alongside your salary and uncapped earning potential, you will receive 25 days’ annual leave plus bank holidays, a healthcare scheme, mental wellbeing support, access to 24/7 GP and counselling services, and a generous pension scheme. You will also receive one paid volunteering day each year and have opportunities to win tickets to events at Utilita-sponsored arenas and football matches.
Why work at Utilita?
A schedule that supports your work-life balance.
We understand that a great Smart Meter Engineer role is not just about salary. It is also about having a structured working day and being able to plan your life accordingly.
You will be scheduled an average of 4 jobs per day, with an average travel time to jobs of approximately 35 minutes between appointments.
We aim to schedule your work several weeks in advance, giving you greater visibility of your schedule. This helps you plan life outside work while still giving you the opportunity to take on additional work when it suits you.
First-class training and support.
Your journey will begin at our award-winning training academy in Warrington, where you will receive a comprehensive induction.
You will then receive ongoing mentoring to help you strengthen your knowledge, understand our processes and confidently adapt to the Utilita way of working.
A team that keeps you connected.
We understand that working in the field can sometimes feel isolating, which is why creating a connected and supportive environment is so important to us.
Through regular manager check-ins, access to technical experts, collaborative colleague networks and ongoing communication, you'll always have the support you need and someone to turn to throughout your working day.
What you will be doing.
As a Dual Fuel Smart Meter Engineer, you will represent Utilita in customers’ homes, installing smart meters safely and professionally across domestic properties.
You will play an important role in delivering our customer-first approach, providing a positive experience while maintaining high standards of safety, quality and service.
What we need from you.
To be considered for this opportunity, you will need:
• Smart Metering qualifications, including CCN1 or CMA1 and MET1, or equivalent.
• At least 12 months experience working as a Dual Fuel Smart Meter Engineer.
• A valid full UK driving licence.
Who are Utilita?
Founded in 2003, Utilita Energy was created to challenge the Big Six energy suppliers by offering a fair and flexible service that is good for both the pocket and the planet.
As the first supplier to install a Smart Meter back in 2005 and kick-start Britain’s smart meter revolution, we continue to invest in smart technology and look for new ways to improve our services through innovation.
We are also committed to sustainability, with an ambition to become a Net Zero business by 2030. We believe everyone can make a meaningful impact through small, positive changes.
Our values are simple but powerful:
Fairness. Smart. Sustainability.
Our employees and customers come from all walks of life. We are committed to championing diversity, creating an inclusive culture and providing an environment where you can be your authentic self.
Utilita is part of the Luxion group which comprises Luxion Group Ltd, Utilita Energy Ltd, Luxion Sales Ltd, Utilita Field Services Ltd, Procode Technology Ltd and Canary Care Global Ltd.

The Medical Monitor, Clinical Development is responsible for providing day‑to‑day medical oversight for one or more clinical trials to ensure patient safety, data integrity, and protocol compliance throughout trial execution. This role serves as the primary medical point of contact for study teams and clinical sites, supporting safe and compliant study conduct in alignment with Good Clinical Practice (GCP) and regulatory requirements.
Operating within defined protocols and development strategies, the Medical Monitor provides medical judgment during trial execution, including safety signal evaluation, eligibility assessments, dose modifications, and risk mitigation. The role works closely with Clinical Operations, Pharmacovigilance, Data Management, Biostatistics, and Regulatory Affairs to support operational excellence, timely issue resolution, and high‑quality clinical data.
GE HealthCare is a leading global medical technology and digital solutions innovator. Our purpose is to create a world where healthcare has no limits. Unlock your ambition, turn ideas into world-changing realities, and join an organization where every voice makes a difference, and every difference builds a healthier world.

Ce poste constitue le principal point de contact médical pour les équipes de l’étude et les sites cliniques, en veillant à ce que les études soient menées de manière sûre et conforme aux Bonnes Pratiques Cliniques (BPC/GCP) ainsi qu’aux exigences réglementaires.

Job Description:
Craft Apprenticeship - Surface Finish Fitter
Start date: September 2027
Location: Broughton
Duration: 36 months
Application closing date: We encourage you to apply early to avoid missing out on this opportunity! Please note we will close adverts as soon as we receive sufficient applications.
Salary :  A competitive starting salary of £19,185
Comprehensive benefits package, including a company pension, generous holiday allowance plus bank holidays, and our 'Success Share' scheme, allowing you to participate in the company's performance. You'll also have access to a wide range of flexible benefits to support your well-being.
Work-life balance is important, with a 35-hour week on either a standard working day or a double-day shift pattern, providing flexibility.
About us
Ready to build the wings that lift the world? Join Airbus as a Craft Surface finish Apprentice in Airbus Broughton and play a vital role in manufacturing wings for our A320, A330, and A350 aircraft families. This 36-month program offers valuable hands-on training, recognised qualifications, and a clear path to a rewarding career in aviation."
At Airbus, we believe a diverse workforce drives innovation. We're committed to fostering an inclusive environment where everyone feels valued and empowered to thrive.  Airbus is a global pioneer in the aerospace industry, leading the way in designing, manufacturing, and delivering aerospace products across Commercial Aircraft, Helicopters, Defence, and Space sectors. As the global center of excellence for wing manufacturing, our Broughton site delivers over 500 wing sets annually. Our apprenticeship programs are carefully designed to give you valuable practical training alongside your academic studies, setting you up for success and helping your career truly fly.
With over 17,5000 employees worldwide and as the largest aeronautics and space company in Europe, Airbus is at the forefront of the aviation industry. During your apprenticeship you will work alongside our experienced engineers and quality team to support you to complete the work safely and efficiently
What you will be doing
As a Craft Surface Finish Fitting apprentice you’ll immerse yourself for the  first 12 months of the programme  learning the foundational skills required in the preparation and application of surface finishes. While completing your academic studies the course will also cover an element of mechanical fitting activities. This program is designed to equip you with valuable qualifications and competencies to work directly on live aircraft. You'll also benefit from our Gen A support network and learning HUB, providing additional support, events, and opportunities for all early career participants.
This 36-month apprenticeship is structured to maximise your learning and impact:
Year One: You will spend the first 12  months of your apprenticeship based at Rhyl College, working towards obtaining:
•
NVQ Level 2 diploma in Performing Engineering Operations;
•
Level 2 Academic Qualification
•
Level 2 Essential Skills;
This will allow you to develop the necessary skills, knowledge and experience to enable you to make an immediate contribution when you enter the workforce in the second year.
Year 2 and 3:  Your Learning Takes Flight at Broughton! Building on your foundational knowledge, you'll join our world-class team at the Airbus Broughton site in North Wales. Here, you'll apply your skills directly to live aircraft projects and assist in the preparation and painting of the wings for our Single Aisle and Wide body families. Your varied tasks will require a range of technical skills. This will include:
•
Preparation & Setup: This involves meticulously cleaning, sanding, and masking surfaces to ensure proper adhesion and a flawless finish. It also includes accurately mixing paints and preparing spray equipment according to specifications.
•
Application & Quality: Skillfully applying multiple, even coats of paint using precise techniques, while monitoring environmental conditions. A crucial part of the role is inspecting the finish for quality, making adjustments, and performing touch-ups, all while strictly adhering to safety protocols and equipment maintenance.
•
Fitting Activities - This would include a placement in our single aisle and wide body business areas to perform fitting activities in our wingbox production areas, these activities will include drilling and installing fasteners.
You'll continue your academic studies on day release, working towards:
•
Level 3 NVQ Extended Diploma (Aeronautical Engineering)
•
Level 3 Academic Certificate
Upon successful completion of your 38-month apprenticeship, you'll become a skilled Surface finish Fitter, specialising in the preparation and application of surface finishes plus the ability to drill-off and assembly of both metallic and composite components to produce the wing box structure on our world-class Airbus aircraft. You'll receive a Modern Apprenticeship Certificate, setting you up for a fantastic career.
Requirements
To be eligible, you must achieve a minimum of 5 GCSEs (Grade C or 4), including: Maths, English Language, Double Award Science (Grade CC/ 44) OR Single award in Physics (C/4) plus 2 additional GCSEs (other equivalent or higher qualifications may be considered)
To be a successful candidate you need to:
•
Have a passion for learning, enjoy hands-on, teamwork and problem solving activities
•
Include your CV stating your predicted or achieved grades in your application;
•
Include your Cover Letter stating your motivation for this role in your application.
Important Information:
GRADES:  Please note: Any offer will be conditional upon us receiving evidence of your required grades by August 31, 2027, in addition to completing all pre-employment checks and online forms.
RIGHT TO WORK IN THE UK: Candidates must have current legal authorisation to work in the United Kingdom. For more information, please check the Government Website.
